F6-39.genai_enabler: Standing up and operating a merchant presence that survives casual review now costs almost nothing: storefront content, product catalogues, support correspondence and transaction narratives can all be generated. Being the merchant, rather than attacking one, becomes the economically rational play.
F6-39.description: The merchant is the destination. Proceeds are pushed through a merchant of record the attacker controls, and emerge as ordinary settlement for goods that were never shipped. Each authorisation is well-formed and the customers may even be genuine, which is what makes this hard: nothing about the payment itself is anomalous. The evidence lies in the merchant profile, in the mismatch between declared and realised behaviour, and in the bipartite structure of who transacts there.
preconditions: Merchant onboarding can be completed on submitted evidence with limited ongoing monitoring.
No continuous comparison of realised transaction mix against the declared category.

observable_signals.signal: Realised transaction mix does not match the category the merchant registered under.
Merchant is young relative to the volume and ticket size it processes.
Customer base is narrow and repetitive in a way no genuine retailer sustains.
Merchant clusters with other entities sharing registration and settlement characteristics.
Amounts are unusually uniform and unusually round for the declared category.

mitigations: Monitor realised transaction mix against the declared category continuously, not at onboarding.
Hold settlement for new merchants until behavioural history accumulates.
Cluster merchants on registration and settlement evidence and review clusters together.
references: FATF - Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Red Flag Indicators
Mastercard Rules - merchant onboarding and monitoring obligations

F6-40.name: Stored-value and gift-card cash-out chains
F6-40.actor: An operator converting compromised payment authority into stored-value instruments that can be resold or redeemed away from the original rail.
F6-40.genai_enabler: Purchasing, tracking and reselling stored-value instruments at volume is clerical work, and clerical work is what agents are best at. The conversion step that used to bound this fraud is no longer a bottleneck.
F6-40.description: Stored value is attractive because it severs the link between the compromised credential and the eventual benefit: once value sits on an instrument, the payment rail has nothing left to trace. The purchases themselves are ordinary ecommerce transactions in an unremarkable category. What is detectable is the concentration, the timing relative to account compromise, and the mismatch against the customer historical category profile.
preconditions: Stored-value instruments purchasable without additional verification.
Rapid redemption or transfer permitted after purchase.

observable_signals.signal: Sudden concentration of spend into stored-value categories with no history of it.
Multiple purchases in quick succession from one customer or agent.
Amounts cluster on denominations rather than following a natural spend distribution.
Purchasers across unrelated accounts converge on a small set of redeeming entities.

mitigations: Apply step-up authentication to stored-value purchases above a low threshold.
Delay redemption for newly purchased instruments.
Monitor convergence of unrelated purchasers onto shared redeeming entities.
references: FATF - Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Red Flag Indicators
FBI IC3 - public service announcements on gift card fraud

F6-41.name: Cross-border micro-remittance layering
F6-41.actor: An operator dispersing value across borders in amounts small enough to sit below per-transaction reporting and review thresholds.
F6-41.genai_enabler: Splitting value across many corridors, currencies and counterparties while respecting each jurisdiction thresholds is a constraint-satisfaction problem. Agents solve it continuously and re-plan as corridors close, which is what makes the dispersion adaptive rather than static.
F6-41.description: Value crosses borders as a large number of small transfers, each below the threshold that would attract attention, spread across corridors so that no single jurisdiction sees enough to act. The defeat of this pattern is aggregation: individually the transfers are invisible, and in aggregate the cross-border share of one entity activity is wildly out of line with its peers.
preconditions: Cross-border transfers available at low value with per-transaction reporting thresholds.
No aggregation of activity across corridors or counterparties.

observable_signals.signal: Cross-border share of activity is far above the norm for comparable customers.
Amounts sit consistently just below reporting thresholds.
Counterparties are spread across many corridors with no economic relationship.
Aggregate value moved is a severe outlier against the customer own history.

mitigations: Aggregate across corridors and counterparties before applying thresholds.
Score cross-border share relative to a peer group rather than in absolute terms.
Alert on dispersion patterns that no legitimate economic relationship explains.
references: FATF - Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Red Flag Indicators
RBI - Master Direction on Liberalised Remittance Scheme reporting

F6-42.name: Subscription-farm bleed
F6-42.actor: An operator monetising compromised payment authority through many small recurring charges rather than a single large one.
F6-42.genai_enabler: Creating and operating many plausible subscription products, each with its own billing descriptor and support presence, is generation work. The result is a monetisation channel that is individually beneath notice and collectively substantial, sustained over months.
F6-42.description: Rather than extracting value at once, the attacker bleeds it: small recurring charges spread across many merchant descriptors and many victims, each below the threshold at which a customer bothers to dispute. Recurring rails are designed for exactly this cadence, so the charges look entirely correct. What is anomalous is the sudden appearance of several unrelated new subscriptions on one credential, and the sharing of those descriptors across customers who have nothing else in common.
preconditions: Recurring authority can be established without a fresh consent event per merchant.
Low-value recurring charges are not routinely surfaced to the customer.

observable_signals.signal: Several new recurring authorities appear on one credential in a short window.
Charge amounts sit below the value at which customers typically dispute.
Descriptors are shared across customers with no other connection to each other.
Recurring cadence is machine-exact in a way genuine billing rarely is.

mitigations: Require a fresh consent event per recurring merchant, not per credential.
Surface a consolidated view of active recurring authorities to the customer.
Cluster billing descriptors and review those appearing across unrelated customers.
references: Mastercard Rules - recurring payment and negative option billing obligations
RBI Master Direction on Digital Payment Security Controls - recurring mandates
